gaps.quote: A disk array has coefficients of modulus below $1$
gaps.note: The paper (line 2786) defines a disk array as one of norm at most one, i.e. coefficient modulus at most 1, not strictly below 1. The page's strict definition is stronger than the paper's and is not what the grid-array bounds (coefficients of absolute value at most 2^p before scaling) and the contraction/truncation steps use.

gaps.quote: By bilinearity of $P$ and the disk bound on both operands
gaps.note: The page never states that the pointwise product satisfies ||P(x,y)||_inf <= ||x||_inf ||y||_inf (the paper, lines 3448-3450, takes it from the signed-ring-product lemma). Bilinearity alone gives only the splitting P(u~-u,v~)+P(u,v~-v); the bound 2 delta needs this contraction property of P, which the page states only for M_r.

gaps.quote: Since the opposite transform $\mathcal T_+$ is a contraction with its own error $\delta$
gaps.note: The page gives only the cost of a transform. That T_+ is a contraction, that the returned opposite output is within delta of T_+ applied to the (disk grid) input z~, are asserted without being stated anywhere on the page; the reader cannot check the 3 delta + eta bound (paper lines 3464-3470, from the transform lemma at about line 2975).
